writeup.headline: Rubrik rates Hold: fast growth, net cash and strong momentum offset by very high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Rubrik scores 57, a Hold, with strengths and weaknesses roughly cancelling out. Growth is strong (score 84), with revenue up 37.9% year on year in the latest quarter and up 42.5% on a trailing basis, though growth slowed by 1.1 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet (96) is net cash, with cash covering debt 1.54 times, and the trend (90) is powerful: the shares are 54.7% above their 200-day average, 111.3 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and 9.5% below their 52-week high. Against that, valuation scores just 4. In absolute terms the multiples are high: 15.2x sales and 77.2x free cash flow, with an FCF yield 3.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and EV/EBIT is not meaningful because EBIT is negative. There is no comparison with its own history. Quality is middling at 42: an 80.2% gross margin and 19.7% FCF margin sit alongside a -18.3% operating margin, stock-based pay at 22.2% of revenue and diluted shares up 5.8% year on year.
key_risks: High absolute valuation (15.2x sales, 77.2x FCF) leaves little room for any growth disappointment.
Still unprofitable on an operating basis (-18.3% margin), with stock-based compensation at 22.2% of revenue.
Ongoing dilution, with diluted shares up 5.8% year on year.
After a sharp run (54.7% above the 200-day average), momentum could reverse quickly.
Competition in AI-agent data protection, including Cohesity's rival product; new Rubrik AI tools are only in private preview.
what_would_change: A rise of 8 points to 65 would move the rating to Buy, most plausibly from improving quality (operating losses narrowing, less SBC and dilution) or a lower valuation after a price pullback with growth intact.
A fall of 13 points below 45 would mean Sell, for example if trend momentum breaks down and growth decelerates sharply.
Positive news flow, such as further guidance raises or verified analyst upgrades, could lift the news risk score of 55.
Confidence would firm once valuation history reaches 24 month-ends (currently 20).
